presentingComplaint: 3 days of tingling and mild weakness in both legs, with unsteadiness on the stairs.
history: Previously well 34-year-old software engineer. Ten to fourteen days ago had a self-limiting diarrhoeal illness (loose stools for ~4 days, no blood, resolved without treatment). Over the last 3 days he has noticed symmetrical 'pins-and-needles' in both feet spreading to the calves, aching low back and thigh pain, and mild difficulty rising from a chair and climbing stairs. Still fully ambulant and self-caring. No breathlessness, no swallowing or speech difficulty, no double vision, no bladder or bowel disturbance, no fever. No recent travel, no new drugs, no vaccination, no toxin/alcohol exposure. This is an early, mild, still-ambulant presentation rather than the classic fulminant flaccid quadriparesis.
examination: Alert, comfortable, afebrile, well perfused. Cranial nerves normal; no facial or bulbar weakness. Symmetrical mild lower-limb weakness (MRC grade 4/5 proximally and distally), upper limbs grade 5. Distal-to-proximal sensory tingling with subtly reduced pinprick in a stocking distribution. Ankle jerks absent and knee jerks depressed bilaterally; upper-limb reflexes reduced. Plantars flexor. No sensory level, no spinal tenderness, no sphincter disturbance. Gait cautious but independent. Single-breath count 30.

labs.csfWBC: 2 /µL (albuminocytological dissociation; may still be normal in first week)

imaging: MRI whole spine with contrast: no cord compression, no cord signal change; may show subtle contrast enhancement of anterior nerve roots/cauda equina supporting inflammatory polyradiculopathy.
microbiology: Stool culture from the antecedent illness not obtained; Campylobacter jejuni serology may be positive. No active infection on current bloods.
differentialDiagnoses: Guillain-Barré syndrome (acute inflammatory demyelinating polyradiculoneuropathy) — antecedent GI illness, ascending symmetric weakness with areflexia, albuminocytological dissociation
Compressive myelopathy / cauda equina — excluded by absence of sensory level and normal MRI spine
Multiple sclerosis / transverse myelitis — CNS pattern, would expect UMN signs
Myasthenia gravis — fatigable weakness, but reflexes preserved and no bulbar/ocular signs
Hypokalaemic periodic paralysis — excluded by normal potassium
finalDiagnosis: Early Guillain-Barré syndrome (AIDP), mild/ambulant stage, post-Campylobacter
citations: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine 22e — Guillain-Barré Syndrome and Other Immune-Mediated Neuropathies
Peripheral Nerve Society / GBS-CIDP Foundation — Guillain-Barré Syndrome Diagnosis and Management Guideline — 2023
Brighton Collaboration — Case Definition for Guillain-Barré Syndrome
contraindications: Do NOT give corticosteroids — no benefit in GBS and may harm
Avoid discharging without serial respiratory monitoring — weakness can progress rapidly over hours to days
Caution with drugs causing autonomic or respiratory depression
edgeCases: Miller-Fisher variant (ophthalmoplegia, ataxia, areflexia) with anti-GQ1b antibodies
Rapid progression to respiratory failure (falling FVC/single-breath count) requiring intubation
Autonomic instability with labile BP and arrhythmias
Normal CSF protein in the first week does not exclude GBS — repeat if needed
expectedMaiK: Recognise early GBS from antecedent infection plus ascending symmetric weakness with areflexia; admit for serial respiratory (FVC/single-breath count) and autonomic monitoring, confirm with CSF and nerve conduction studies, and start IVIg or plasma exchange if progressive or non-ambulant. Not an infection — no antibiotics.
expectedNextQuestions: Any antecedent diarrhoeal or respiratory infection in the past 4 weeks?
Any breathlessness, difficulty swallowing, slurred speech, or double vision?
How fast is the weakness progressing (hours vs days)?
Any bladder/bowel disturbance or a sensory level (to exclude cord pathology)?
Any recent vaccination, new medication, or toxin exposure?
expectedInvestigations: Bedside forced vital capacity and single-breath count (serial)
Lumbar puncture — CSF for albuminocytological dissociation
MRI whole spine with contrast to exclude cord compression
Anti-ganglioside antibodies (anti-GM1, anti-GQ1b) and Campylobacter serology
regressionAssertions: Must recommend serial respiratory monitoring (FVC / single-breath count)
Must recommend CSF analysis and nerve conduction studies
Must consider and exclude cord compression via MRI spine
Must NOT recommend antibiotics or corticosteroids
